headline: At 30 June 2025 Australia had 228,259 operational residential aged care places. That is 66.1 places for every 1,000 people aged 70 or over, using the ABS estimated resident population. Holding the long-standing planning benchmark of 78 would take another 40,939 places today. The ratio was 81.7 in 2015, and the place gap against that benchmark has grown by 49,854 places. Last year the stocktake shows a net change of 794 operational places. States have said about 10,600 new places a year are needed.

kpis.label: Places for every 1,000 people aged 70+
kpis.takeaway: The planning benchmark used here is 78. The published Department ratio, on an older population base, is 67.0.

kpis.label: Places still needed to reach 78 per 1,000
kpis.takeaway: This is today's gap if the stock of places does not change. It is not a count of people on a waiting list.

kpis.label: Net operational places added last year
kpis.takeaway: States, quoted by the ABC, said about 800 beds were added last year and about 10,600 a year are needed. The stocktake is the counted change in operational places.

kpis.label: Extra places a year to hold today's ratio to 2031
kpis.unit: ABS medium projection, places frozen at 2025
kpis.takeaway: Reaching 78 per 1,000 by 2031, from today's stock, would take about 16,963 extra places a year.

kpis.label: Largest regional gap against 78 per 1,000
kpis.takeaway: Its published ratio is 69.0 places per 1,000 people aged 70+. The lowest ratio is Darwin (Northern Territory) at 34.7.

sa_hospital_patients_waiting.label: More than 500
sa_hospital_patients_waiting.comparison_when: four years earlier (around October 2022, SA Health figures reported in September 2026)
sa_hospital_patients_waiting.statement: More than 500 older patients are in South Australian public hospitals waiting for a residential aged care placement, up from about 60 four years ago.

sources.title: Hospitals 'paying the price' for lack of federal action on aged care, SA Premier says
Australia's aged care bed crisis hits boiling point for families waiting years

national_places_needed_per_year.statement: South Australia's Health Minister said at least 10,600 additional federal residential aged care places are needed nationally each year over the next two decades.
national_places_needed_per_year.source: ABC News, 9 November 2026, quoting SA Health Minister Blair Boyer

national_places_added_last_year_reported.statement: The same minister said that last year just 800 beds were added to the system.
national_places_added_last_year_reported.source: ABC News, 9 November 2026, quoting SA Health Minister Blair Boyer

federal_construction_claim.statement: A federal spokesperson told the ABC the government is supporting the construction of around 5,000 additional residential aged care beds nationally each year.

notes.population: ABS Estimated Resident Population, persons, 30 June, single year of age 70 to 100 summed. Age 100 is the top code returned by ERP_Q for this extract.
notes.projections: ABS Population Projections, Australia, 2022 base to 2071, series 29 (medium / series B), persons. State tables B1–B8 and Australia table B9. Growth from the medium series is applied to the 2025 ERP.
notes.places: Department of Health stocktake of operational residential places, which include flexible residential places in Multi-Purpose Services, the Innovative Pool and the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Flexible Aged Care Program. These are operational places, not occupied beds and not vacancies.
notes.acpr_population: Aged Care Planning Regions are not an ABS geography. The 2025 regional population is the Department's own June 2025 projection implied by its published places and ratio (revised projections based on the 2017 ERP). The 80+ figure applies the state's ABS share of people aged 80+ within the 70+ population. The 2031 regional population keeps each region's 2025 share of its state and grows it with the state's ABS medium-series 70+ growth.
notes.benchmark: 78 residential places per 1,000 people aged 70+ is the residential component of the long-standing Commonwealth target provision ratio. It is a planning yardstick. Home care places have been assigned to people rather than services since February 2017 and are not in this residential benchmark.
notes.hospitals: Hospital waiting figures are quoted from ABC reports of state sources. They are not calculated from the aged care datasets.
